Subject: Immediate capacity ask + how will overages reconcile for our launch

Hi Tessa,

We kicked off a staggered rollout for AtlasAI Search on Friday and are seeing a much larger-than-expected spike. Our infra team is forecasting ~3x token throughput over the next 72 hours (mostly inference for rerank + embeddings).

We need two things urgently: 1) a short-term uplift in quota/rate limits for the next 7 days to avoid throttling, and 2) clarity on how any overrun will be billed — we need to propose numbers to our CFO and Procurement.

What options do you have for temporary credit/financing, or a staged true-up so we don’t get hit with a surprise invoice? We can sign a PO if that helps speed approval (I can loop procurement).

Thanks,
Samir

Samir — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the launch momentum. I copied Ben and Laura to help with pricing and procurement flow.

High level — we can do a 7-day uplift immediately. Two commercial paths we typically offer for short launches:

- Option A (Prepaid uplift + discount): Advance a temporary headroom of N tokens / provisional throughput for 7 days on a prepaid PO. We apply a 10% uplift discount on the incremental volume and reconcile true usage at month end (overage applied only if usage exceeds the uplift).

- Option B (Provisional uplift + deferred true-up): We open an emergency headroom for 7 days with no upfront charge; we capture the overrun and amortize it across the next 2 invoices with a staged discount (5% off the uplift portion) and the ability to convert to a committed slab if you want. This requires a short purchase commitment (signed addendum) to avoid abuse.

Operational items we need to move fast:
- A short email from Procurement approving either Option A or B (PO number or intent).
- A rough expected uplift (tokens/day or QPS) so we size the headroom.
- Contact for billing so we can route the PO + amendment.

If you want, Ben can propose a blended number (discount + amortization) that lands near your CFO’s tolerance. Laura, can you outline typical PO language and timing? Ben, I think a 7-day emergency uplift with Option B amortized over two invoices with a small onboarding credit could work — any pushback?

I’ll stand by to open the uplift once we get purchase intent.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Immediate capacity ask + how will overages reconcile for our launch

Samir / team — quick commercial proposal to accelerate approvals.

We can do a hybrid: emergency uplift (no upfront invoice) for 7 days + a one-time launch credit and a staged true-up. Proposed terms: 
- Emergency uplift ceiling: +300% of baseline token volume for 7 days.
- Launch credit: $12,000 applied to overrun reconciliation (one-off credit so your net exposure is reduced).
- True-up: any usage beyond the uplift ceiling is billed at standard overrun rates but amortized across the next 2 invoices. We will cap the amortized invoice uplift at 40% of the monthly invoice to limit spikes to your cashflow.
- If you convert to a 6-month committed slab at the end of the month, we will offer a 12% retroactive credit on the uplifted volume (applied to the following invoice).

Operational asks from Procurement: PO referencing "Emergency Uplift — D-3852" and a signature on the SLA amendment (I can attach a redline). Laura, please confirm standard PO text and any legal turnaround expectations.

Samir — if you can shoot over the PO (even as a draft), I’ll queue the uplift today. If procurement needs a short note to the CFO explaining amortization and cap, I can draft it and include an example invoice schedule.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
